skill.name: wp-playground
skill.description: Guide agents through WordPress Playground CLI and browser workflows for disposable WordPress testing, blueprints, snapshots, version switching, and Xdebug debugging.
skill.summary: Run disposable WordPress Playground instances for testing, blueprints, snapshots, and debugging.
skill.author: Automattic

security_audit.summary: The audit found no prompt injection or malicious exfiltration instructions. Most hardcoded URL and markdown backtick findings are documentation examples or official WordPress references. The real risks are user-approved external CLI execution, unpinned @latest npm usage, host path mounting, and blueprint local file access.

remediation.suggestion: Pin @wp-playground/cli to a reviewed version, request user confirmation, and avoid automatic execution from untrusted workspaces.

remediation.issue: Blueprints may use remote sources and local file access
remediation.suggestion: Require trusted blueprint URLs or reviewed local files before running with adjacent file access enabled.

remediation.issue: Broad host mounts can expose secrets
remediation.suggestion: Mount only needed directories and state that projects must exclude credentials, dumps, and production data before launch.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned npm CLI Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to run npx @wp-playground/cli@latest. This can download and execute the current npm package at runtime, so version pinning and user confirmation are important.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command text explicitly uses @latest in multiple npx examples. The behavior is legitimate, but the supply-chain risk is clear and context-specific.

semantic_findings.title: Blueprint Local File Access Requires Trust
semantic_findings.description: The skill permits --blueprint-may-read-adjacent-files for local blueprint assets. This can expose nearby files if a user applies the flag to an untrusted blueprint or broad directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The same local file access flag appears in the main workflow and troubleshooting guidance. The risk depends on user choices, but the capability is explicit.

content.value_statement: WordPress developers need fast, disposable test sites without maintaining a full local stack. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through WordPress Playground setup, blueprints, snapshots, and debugging.
actual_capabilities: Starts local Playground workflows with auto-mounted plugin or theme directories.
Explains manual mount options for multiple plugins, mu-plugins, and custom content.
Runs, reviews, and troubleshoots Playground Blueprints for setup and CI validation.
Builds snapshot workflows for sharing reproducible WordPress environments.
Guides WordPress and PHP version switching for compatibility checks.
Provides Xdebug setup guidance for plugin and theme debugging.
limitations: It depends on Node.js 20.18 or newer and npm or npx availability.
It cannot make Playground suitable for workloads needing native database access or unsupported PHP extensions.
It should not run untrusted blueprints, npm packages, or mounted projects without user review.
It does not replace full production parity testing for complex hosting environments.

use_cases.title: Test Plugin Changes
use_cases.description: Launch a disposable Playground instance, mount a plugin, and verify activation without setting up a database or web server.

use_cases.title: Reproduce Compatibility Bugs
use_cases.description: Pin WordPress and PHP versions, run targeted checks, and document whether a bug appears in a clean instance.

use_cases.title: Share Demo Snapshots
use_cases.description: Build a shareable Playground snapshot that captures a setup for bug reports, review, or customer support.

prompt_templates.title: Start Local Playground
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a WordPress Playground for this plugin. First check prerequisites, then show the launch command and verification steps before executing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Run A Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Playground blueprint and run it locally. Use verbose output, report failed steps, and keep local file access disabled unless needed.

prompt_templates.title: Debug With Xdebug
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a Playground debugging session for this theme. Use Xdebug, confirm path mappings, and list a concise breakpoint test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Build Snapshot Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible snapshot workflow for CI. Include version pins, trusted asset sources, cleanup checks, and a short manual verification checklist.

output_examples.input: I need to test a plugin in a clean WordPress instance.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a readiness check, a local launch plan, and activation checks for the mounted plugin.

output_examples.input: My blueprint fails when installing assets.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies likely failed steps, suggests verbose reruns, and separates trusted remote assets from local file access.

output_examples.input: I need a snapshot for a support ticket.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a repeatable snapshot flow, includes version pinning, and lists checks before sharing the archive.

best_practices: Pin WordPress, PHP, and CLI versions when reproducing bugs or preparing CI workflows.
Use trusted blueprint sources and review steps before allowing local file access.
Keep mounted projects free of secrets, credentials, and production data.
anti_patterns: Running unreviewed public blueprint URLs with local file access enabled.
Mounting an entire project when a plugin, theme, or narrow directory is enough.
Using Playground results as proof for production systems that need native services.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents use WordPress Playground for local testing, blueprints, snapshots, version switching, and debugging.

faq.question: Does it install WordPress locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses WordPress Playground, which runs WordPress in WebAssembly with SQLite.

faq.question: Can it test my plugin or theme?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide auto-mount or manual mount workflows for plugin and theme testing.

faq.question: Does it support browser-only workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain Playground URLs, blueprint links, and the live Blueprint Editor.

faq.question: What should I check before running commands?
faq.answer: Confirm Node.js 20.18 or newer, review mounted paths, and remove secrets from files that Playground can read.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production data?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that Playground instances are ephemeral and should not use production data.
